$comment: Per-million-token prices in USD. EVERY dollar figure contextbill reports derives from
this file, so it is versioned, dated, and cited in the report footer.
Source: Anthropic's published pricing page, read on the date in `dated` below:
https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing
These are Claude API / Microsoft Foundry / Claude Platform on AWS rates. Amazon
Bedrock and Google Vertex AI are partner-operated and priced separately -- contextbill
does not model them.
Figures here are what usage WOULD cost metered at these rates. Most Claude Code usage
is on a subscription, which bills a flat fee, so a contextbill total values the usage
rather than restating an invoice. Every surface says so.
If you are reading a report and the numbers look wrong, check `dated` below first.
A test fails once this table is more than 60 days old.
2026-09-03: every model rate and both cache multipliers below were re-read against the
source above and NONE had moved. `dated` is bumped because the table was re-verified on
that date, not because a price changed -- bumping it without re-reading is the one thing
that turns this field into a lie.
Cache writes are billed as a multiple of the model's base input rate.
5-minute TTL writes at 1.25x; 1-hour TTL writes at 2x.
TRANSCRIPTS DO NOT RECORD WHICH TTL WAS USED. `cache_creation_input_tokens` is a
single number with no TTL field, so contextbill cannot infer it and does not guess.
Default is the 5-minute rate, which is the conservative choice: if your client
actually used 1-hour caching, the reported cost is an UNDERSTATEMENT, never an
overstatement. Override with --cache-ttl=1h. The report always names which was used.

$comment-retired-models: The table below also prices retired models, because old transcripts still mention
them. Without an entry they land in unpricedModels and drop out of the total, which
understates any corpus with history. Keys are post-normalizeModelId: the dated suffix
is stripped before lookup, so `claude-opus-4-1-20250805` resolves to `claude-opus-4-1`.
This note sits outside `models` deliberately -- a `$comment` key inside that map would
be indistinguishable from a model to anything that iterates it.
$comment-missing-fable-5-1: Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 are published ($10 input / $50 output, same as
the 5.0 entries below) and are DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Their cache hits bill at 0.025x the
base input rate, not the 0.1x every other model uses, and `cacheReadMultiplier` above is
a single global number with no per-model override. Adding them would price their cache
reads FOUR TIMES too high, confidently, with nothing failing -- and cache reads are the
largest token class on a real corpus, so that error would dominate any total containing
them. Left unpriced, they land in `unpricedModelsSeen` and are reported loudly instead.
Adding them correctly means giving a model entry its own optional cacheReadMultiplier
and teaching cost.ts to prefer it; do that first, then add the two entries.
$comment-rate-periods: A model entry may carry a `periods` array so usage is priced at the rate in force when
it happened rather than at today's rate. Without it, a vendor price change silently
reprices history and last quarter's report changes value on a re-run.
Shape: `periods: [{ from: 'YYYY-MM-DD', input, output, fastInput?, fastOutput?, note }]`,
`from` inclusive and UTC, each period running until the next one's `from`. The LAST
period must restate the flat `input`/`output` beside it -- those stay the current rate,
so anything that has not been taught about periods still prices at today's rate. A price
change is a NEW period; never edit an existing one, because that is the silent repricing
NO MODEL BELOW CARRIES A PERIOD, and that is a finding rather than an omission. A period
is a claim about what a vendor charged on a date, and this repo can evidence no such
change yet. The one candidate was Sonnet 5: the table read $3/$15 until 2026-08-28 and
now reads $2/$10. That was THIS TABLE being wrong, not a rate that moved -- the scheduled
increase to $3/$15 was cancelled, so $2/$10 was the price the whole time and $3/$15 was
never charged to anyone. Writing it as a dated period would put a rate into the history
that never existed, and every turn before 2026-08-28 would then be priced 50% high with
full confidence. An invented historical rate is worse than no history.
Add a period only with a dated published source in its `note`, and re-derive the pricing
anchor in pipeline.test.ts by hand in the same commit if fixture timestamps cross it.

claude-opus-5.note: Fast mode (usage.speed === 'fast') bills at the premium rate.

claude-opus-4-8.note: Fast mode (usage.speed === 'fast') bills at the premium rate.

claude-sonnet-5.note: $2/$10 launched as introductory pricing through 2026-08-31. The scheduled increase to $3/$15 was cancelled and $2/$10 is now the standard price. Deliberately NOT a dated period: this table carried $3/$15 by mistake until 2026-08-28, and that increase never took effect, so there is no earlier rate to date.

$comment: Model IDs that appear in transcripts but carry no billable rate. Counted
separately and shown in the report rather than silently priced at zero.

$comment-plans: Subscription plan prices for --plan. These are a VENDOR FACT, not a measurement.
contextbill cannot observe what anyone pays, so every figure under `plans` is
copied from a published page on the date in `plans.dated` and is worth exactly
as much as that date. `plans` carries its own `dated` and `source` because plan
prices and API rates move on different schedules and for different reasons.
A plan whose current price cannot be evidenced is OMITTED rather than estimated.
That is safe because the omission is loud: --plan rejects any id absent from
`plans.entries` and prints the ids that are present.
`usdPerMonth` is the MONTHLY-billed price. Where an annual-billed price also
exists it is recorded beside it and is always the lower of the two. The
break-even multiple is computed against the monthly-billed price deliberately:
it is the larger denominator, so it yields the SMALLER multiple. Every choice in
`entries` is nested rather than sitting at the top of `plans` for the same reason
the retired-models note sits outside `models`: a $comment key inside the map
would be indistinguishable from a plan to anything that iterates it.

plans.source: https://claude.com/pricing, re-read 2026-09-03. Max tier split from https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11049741-what-is-the-max-plan, re-read the same day, because the pricing page shows Max only as "From $100" and does not separate 5x from 20x.

pro.label: Claude Pro
pro.note: claude.com/pricing: "$17" per month on an annual subscription, "$20 if billed monthly".

max5.label: Claude Max 5x
max5.note: Anthropic's help centre article on the Max plan gives Max 5x as $100/month and states Max is available as a monthly subscription only, so there is no annual rate to record.

max20.label: Claude Max 20x
max20.note: Same help-centre article: Max 20x is $200/month, monthly billing only. The public pricing page prints only "From $100" for Max and does not distinguish the tiers, which is why the article is cited instead.

team.label: Claude Team, standard seat
team.note: claude.com/pricing, re-read 2026-09-03: the Team standard seat is "$20" per month billed annually and "$25 if billed monthly", for teams of 2 to 150. usdPerMonth is the $25 monthly-billed figure, which is the LARGER denominator and so yields the SMALLER break-even multiple. Priced per seat. contextbill measures one machine, so this compares one person's usage against one seat. Which seat type carries Claude Code depends on how the organisation is configured and contextbill cannot see that -- if you are on a premium seat use --plan team-premium, or the multiple below is five times too large.

team-premium.label: Claude Team, premium seat
team-premium.note: claude.com/pricing, re-read 2026-09-03: the Team premium seat is $100 per month billed annually and $125 if billed monthly. usdPerMonth is the $125 monthly-billed figure, for the same under-claiming reason as the standard seat. Priced per seat, same caveat as the standard seat.

api.label: Claude API, pay as you go
api.note: No subscription fee: usage is billed per token at the rates in `models` above. There is no flat price to divide by, so no break-even multiple exists and none is reported. This is the one plan where the total is an estimate of an invoice rather than a valuation against a fee -- and it is still an estimate, because the cache-write TTL is an assumption.
